brief.headline: Aluminium's backwardation collapsed 84% in a single session to just three dollars while the price barely moved - the scarcity premium is leaving the front of the curve without the price level being repudiated.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: on the 18-September LME official, cash settled $3,285.00, DOWN $18.50 or 0.56%, while three-month settled $3,282.00, down only $3.00 or 0.09%. Because the front fell six times as hard as the forward, the cash-to-three-month backwardation collapsed from $18.50 to $3.00 - the fourth consecutive narrowing. Warehouse stock printed EXACTLY UNCHANGED at 242,600 tonnes, a reported change of zero and the only flat session in the fifteen-session window.

WHY IT MATTERS: a backwardation is what the physical market pays to have metal today rather than in three months. When it drains to nothing while the flat price holds, spot urgency is fading even though forward conviction is not. The stock line says the same thing twice: yesterday's draw was the largest of the window, today there was none at all. Level still near multi-decade lows; marginal rate now nil.

WHY IT IS NOT A MACRO STORY: the dollar index moved 0.02% and the LME euro fixing 0.11%, so there was no currency event. On the identical session COPPER flipped from an $8.50 contango into a $14.00 backwardation and rose 0.74%, and ZINC's backwardation WIDENED from $79.00 to $97.00 on a 1.32% gain. Two peer metals tightened their fronts on the same ring on which aluminium's went flat - which isolates the move to aluminium's own supply picture.

WHAT TO WATCH: Monday 21-September's official is the next data point and the question is binary - does the front re-widen, hold near flat, or cross into outright contango. A crossing would be the first time this cycle that the exchange curve stops paying for immediacy at all. Two dated fundamentals frame it: Chinese August output hit a record 4 Mt, annualising near 47 Mt against a 45 Mt policy ceiling, while Chinese social inventory drew 63,000 tonnes in the week to 18-September on drivers - a Xinjiang logistics bottleneck and pre-holiday restocking - that both expire by design.

kpis.label: LME Cash settlement
kpis.note: THE ENTIRE MOVE WAS IN THE FRONT, AND THE BACKWARDATION HAS ALL BUT DISAPPEARED. LME aluminium cash settled $3,285.00 on 18-September, DOWN $18.50 or 0.56% from $3,303.50, while three-month settled $3,282.00, down only $3.00 or 0.09%. Cash fell six times as hard as three-month, so the cash-to-three-month BACKWARDATION COLLAPSED from $18.50 to $3.00 - an 84% erosion in a single session and the FOURTH CONSECUTIVE NARROWING. Four runs ago this page called a $21.00 spread noise; three runs ago it named the erosion a pattern; today the pattern has effectively completed and the curve is within three dollars of flat. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FACT ON THE PAGE. A backwardation is the physical market paying to have metal now; when it drains away while the flat price barely moves, the scarcity premium is leaving the front of the curve without the price level being repudiated. WAREHOUSE STOCK CONFIRMS IT RATHER THAN CONTRADICTS IT: stock printed EXACTLY UNCHANGED at 242,600 tonnes, a reported change of ZERO and the first zero-change session in the fifteen-session window. Yesterday's 1,000-tonne draw was the largest of the window; today there was none at all. The draw has stalled at precisely the moment the front went flat, and those two facts are the same fact observed twice. THE BOARD IS THE COMPLETE, PUBLISHED LME OFFICIAL FOR FRIDAY 18-SEPTEMBER-2026. This page compiles at about 06:00 London on SATURDAY 19-September. THERE IS NO RING ON A SATURDAY, so the 18-September official is not a lagging figure - it is the last and latest published official, and it is carried deliberately because the market is shut. lme.commentary: THE STORY OF THIS BOARD IS THE FRONT, NOT THE PRICE. Aluminium cash settled $3,285.00 on 18-September, down $18.50 or 0.56%, while three-month settled $3,282.00, down $3.00 or 0.09%. Because cash fell six times as hard as three-month, the cash-to-three-month BACKWARDATION COLLAPSED from $18.50 to $3.00 - the fourth consecutive narrowing and an 84% erosion in one session. The curve is now within three dollars of flat. Stock printed EXACTLY UNCHANGED at 242,600 tonnes, a reported change of zero and the only flat session in the fifteen-session window, immediately after the largest draw of that window. THE BOARD PROVIDES ITS OWN CONTROL GROUP. On the identical session copper flipped from an $8.50 contango into a $14.00 BACKWARDATION and rose 0.74% while drawing 800 tonnes of stock; zinc's backwardation WIDENED from $79.00 to $97.00 and it rose 1.32%. Two peer metals tightened their fronts on the same ring on which aluminium's went flat, and the LME euro fixing moved only 0.11%, so there was no dollar event to blame. That isolates the move to aluminium. THE LEVEL HELD EVEN AS THE STRUCTURE GAVE WAY. Three-month is still $21.00 above the 3,261 line this page has tracked for four runs, and it has now closed above it every session since 15-September. The honest reading is a market whose forward buyers are intact and whose spot urgency has drained: the price is being defended, the scarcity premium is not. Watch Monday's 21-September official for whether the front re-widens, holds near flat, or crosses into outright contango - that crossing, not the flat price, is the event that would change this page's stance.

drivers.text: THE LARGEST TRANCHE OF RETURNING GULF SUPPLY NOW HAS A NUMBER ON IT — Aluminium Bahrain is running at about 1.3 million tonnes annualised, roughly 80% of pre-war capacity, on Lines 4, 5 and 6, with exports via Jeddah on the Red Sea and Sohar in Oman, per its chief executive at the Fastmarkets Budapest conference on 16-September as reported 18-September. Pre-war capacity was around 1.6 Mt. The Q3 record premium was underwritten by the ABSENCE of Gulf tonnes; their measured return is the most direct argument against repeating it.

drivers.text: ASIAN SPOT IS NOT VALIDATING THE CONTRACT LEVEL AND THE CHINESE PHYSICAL MARKET IS SPLIT — Dated September reporting describes Asian premiums as subdued at roughly $320-380/t against a settled Q3 benchmark of $395/t. A discount region inside the world's largest consumer is a direct argument against a premium reset higher.

Because roughly two tonnes of alumina are required per tonne of aluminium and two to three tonnes of bauxite per tonne of alumina, a freight-driven cost move propagates through the chain with a lag rather than immediately. Guinea's export quota policy and the tail of the rainy season remain the two named swing factors. logistics.note: PARTIAL AND CONTESTED EASING, ON THE RECORD FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS WINDOW - AND IT IS NOT UNAMBIGUOUSLY GOOD NEWS FOR THE METAL. Commodity-market reporting captured 18-September cites satellite imagery indicating Saudi Arabia moved about 2.8 million barrels a day through the strait over six days, against roughly 700,000 in August, and records around 60 million barrels sold from Ras Tanura for September-October loading via ship-to-ship transfer OUTSIDE the strait. logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: A SECOND CHOKEPOINT REMAINS IN PLAY AND NOTHING PUBLISHED THIS WEEKEND CHANGED IT. The Houthi group was reported to have seized the port city of Mocha, gaining leverage over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, declaring a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia and striking Saudi energy infrastructure; Bab el-Mandeb transits are down about 24% since the July blockade and MARAD advisory 2026-006 runs to 22-September. THE IMPORTANCE IS ROUTING RATHER THAN VOLUME: Bab el-Mandeb is the alternative on which Hormuz-affected cargo has partly relied, so two contested chokepoints are not twice the risk of one - THEY REMOVE THE SUBSTITUTE. THAT LOGIC NOW RUNS IN REVERSE AND IT IS WORTH SAYING SO: if the Hormuz arrangement reported on 07-September completes, the pressure on Bab el-Mandeb as a substitute route falls at the same time, and the shipping-risk premium embedded in Western delivered prices unwinds from both ends at once. THE PHYSICAL CONTRADICTION ALSO PERSISTS: an 11-September market review reports Middle Eastern ingot supply into Japan as relatively ample and DAMAGED MIDDLE EASTERN CAPACITY AS RECOVERED. headlines.title: THE ALUMINIUM BACKWARDATION COLLAPSED 84% IN ONE SESSION, from $18.50 to $3.00, on the 18-September LME official. Cash fell $18.50 or 0.56% to $3,285.00 while three-month fell only $3.00 or 0.09% to $3,282.00, so the entire move was in the front. This is the fourth consecutive narrowing and it effectively completes a pattern this page named three runs ago. The curve is now within three dollars of flat. The scarcity premium is leaving the front without the price level being repudiated.

THE LME STOCK DRAW STOPPED DEAD AT 242,600 TONNES - a reported change of ZERO, the only flat session in the fifteen-session window, and an immediate reversal of yesterday's 1,000-tonne draw which was the window's largest. A flat print is not a build and must not be read as one, but it removes the daily confirmation that the visible tightness is still being consumed. Stock remains close to multi-decade lows, so the LEVEL is still supportive; it is the RATE that has gone to nothing.

THE BOARD'S OWN CONTROL GROUP CONTRADICTED ALUMINIUM. On the identical 18-September ring, COPPER flipped from an $8.50 CONTANGO into a $14.00 BACKWARDATION, rose 0.74% and drew 800 tonnes of stock; ZINC's backwardation WIDENED from $79.00 to $97.00 on a 1.32% gain with cash clearing $4,000; LEAD rose 0.42%. Only nickel fell, by 1.04%. Two peer fronts tightened on the very session aluminium's went flat, and the dollar index moved 0.02% - which removes the macro explanation and isolates the move to aluminium.

ALUMINIUM BAHRAIN IS RUNNING AT ABOUT 1.3 MILLION TONNES ANNUALISED, ROUGHLY 80% OF PRE-WAR CAPACITY, ON LINES 4, 5 AND 6, its chief executive told Reuters on the sidelines of the Fastmarkets conference in Budapest on 16-September, with the reporting carried on 18-September. Pre-war capacity was around 1.6 Mt. He described damage from the late-March Iranian strike as minor and confirmed exports are moving via Jeddah on the Red Sea and Sohar in Oman. This is the single largest quantified tranche of returning ex-China supply on this page and it is the most plausible published explanation for a front that stopped paying for immediacy.

CHINESE AUGUST PRIMARY OUTPUT HIT A RECORD 4 MILLION TONNES, up 4.7% year on year, with January-August at about 31 million tonnes, up 3.9%, according to National Bureau of Statistics data reported 18-September. At that pace annual output would reach roughly 47 million tonnes, ABOVE the long-standing 45-million-tonne policy ceiling that this page's supply case has rested on for months. A new alumina project in Guangxi also entered trial production, adding to future upstream supply. The ceiling is the thesis; a 47 Mt run-rate is the test of it.

CHINESE ALUMINIUM INGOT SOCIAL INVENTORIES FELL 63,000 TONNES IN THE WEEK TO 18-SEPTEMBER, and 43,000 tonnes from the Monday of that week, with the three major regions recording a combined 26,000-tonne daily destock. Weekly primary production held steady near 874,700 tonnes, which makes this a DEMAND-LED drawdown rather than a supply cut. Social inventories have fallen from roughly 815,000 tonnes in early September to about 776,000 by 14-September and lower since. This is the strongest single bullish datum in the window.

BOTH DRIVERS OF THAT CHINESE DRAWDOWN HAVE BUILT-IN EXPIRY DATES, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The named causes are a Xinjiang logistics bottleneck restricting shipments into coastal hubs - a transport problem, not a production cut, which normalises when transport eases - and pre-holiday restocking ahead of the national holidays, a calendar impulse that ends when the holiday does. Downstream liquid aluminium purchases actually edged LOWER on the week, with the liquid share of total supply down 0.02 percentage points. Tightness that expires on a schedule is not the same as structural tightness.

CHINA'S PHYSICAL MARKET SPLIT THREE WAYS ON 18-SEPTEMBER AND ONE OF THE THREE IS A WARNING. East China was healthiest, with strong warehouse withdrawals and SMM A00 transacting at premiums of RMB 10-30/t, spot A00 assessed at RMB 24,180/t, up RMB 20. South China premiums ran RMB 215-255/t but on constrained physical supply rather than demand strength. CENTRAL CHINA TRADED AT DISCOUNTS OF RMB 30-60/t to futures even as suppliers held quotes firm - end-use demand refusing to validate the headline price.

CAST ALUMINIUM ALLOY SOCIAL INVENTORIES POSTED A FIFTH CONSECUTIVE WEEKLY BUILD TO ABOUT 34,100 TONNES, up from roughly 28,100 tonnes in late August, with separate SMM reporting recording a sixth consecutive build at a slowing pace. This is the second independent signal of weak downstream absorption alongside central China's discount. An ingot line that draws while the alloy line builds is a market moving metal into the chain faster than the chain is consuming it.

SMM ADC12 ROSE RMB 100/t TO RMB 24,350 ON 18-SEPTEMBER, BUT THE CAUSE IS TAX ENFORCEMENT RATHER THAN DEMAND. Audits in central China have suspended reverse-invoicing in some areas, shrinking the pool of COMPLIANT scrap without reducing the physical volume in the market, and pushing secondary producers toward costlier primary or semi-finished feedstock. Foshan's A00-to-extrusion-scrap gap sat at RMB 2,468/t on 17-September; Ningbo port shredded rose to RMB 21,470/t and Tianjin to RMB 21,520/t. A cost-push move reverses when enforcement relaxes.

DATED THIRD-PARTY TECHNICALS FOR THE SAME DAY READ CONSOLIDATION, NOT BREAKOUT. SHFE 2611 settled RMB 24,400, up RMB 180 or 0.74%, inside RMB 24,260-24,440 and above its MA5 (24,187), MA10 (24,307), MA30 (24,082.50) and MA60 (23,656.58), with the MACD histogram at -29.74 and narrowing. The LME three-month CLOSE was quoted at US$3,293.50, up 0.11%, above its MA5, MA10, MA30 and MA60. Suggested core ranges were RMB 23,900-24,600 and US$3,200-3,350. These are closes and kerb marks, NOT the 13:20 official, and are recorded as context only.

A SELL-SIDE NOTE DATED 18-SEPTEMBER PUT A TIGHT ALUMINIUM MARKET THROUGH CALENDAR 2028 ON THE RECORD. Kotak Neo retained a Buy on Vedanta Aluminium with a price target of INR 540 against a market price of INR 416.50 on 18-September, arguing global aluminium markets stay tight through CY2028 because project-execution difficulty limits the pace of new Indonesian supply, and that the market may be underestimating the durability of the upcycle. The stock rose 3.02% on the day but is down about 8% over the past month. Treat it as one dated sell-side view, not consensus.

THE US PRIMARY REBUILD IS BROADER THAN THE SMELTER HEADLINES SUGGEST, per 18-September industry reporting. The US operating smelter count has fallen from about thirty to four over two decades, with 2025 primary output estimated near 660,000 tonnes and heavy import reliance. The rebuild depends not only on restarts but on casting, electrolysis maintenance, scrap processing and metal-quality infrastructure. This is a slow, structural addition to ex-China supply and it is policy-driven; combined with the Magnitude 7 and Century restarts already on this page it is the medium-term counterweight to the deficit case.

BRENT FELL A THIRD SESSION TO ABOUT $103.87 WHILE EUROPEAN GAS ROSE AGAIN TO ABOUT EUR 79.52. Reporting attributes the crude fall to Saudi supply risk easing - satellite imagery indicating about 2.8 million barrels a day through the Strait of Hormuz over six days against roughly 700,000 in August, and some 60 million barrels sold from Ras Tanura for September-October loading outside the strait. Lower crude slowly lowers the carbon cost floor AND signals Gulf de-escalation, which accelerates returning supply. Rising gas raises the cost of the arrangements keeping Alunorte at full rate and Qatalum partly curtailed.

Fourth-quarter FY26 revenue rose 25.2% year-on-year to MYR 204.8 million (USD 50.8 million) from MYR 163.5 million (USD 40.5 million), on higher sales volumes in the group's extrusion and fabrication segment; the company reports its strongest quarterly revenue and profit of the financial year, with the headline putting quarterly profit up about 200% to roughly USD 4.5 million. A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. SMM's 24-August daily describes Chinese downstream processing operating rates as under pressure with pre-peak-season stockpiling absent, and Chinese billet inventory is at a five-year seasonal high. A South-East Asian extruder posting 25% revenue growth and its best quarter of the year says the weakness is not uniform across Asia - which is consistent with the trade-flow story on this board, where South-East Asia is being consolidated as the major supplementary scrap source by the UAE export ban and EU tariff increase. earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

NALCO IS THE MOST FULLY INTEGRATED PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL - IT MINES ITS OWN BAUXITE, REFINES ITS OWN ALUMINA AND SMELTS - AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS PRINT IS USEFUL RATHER THAN JUST GOOD. Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

trade.note: TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN CHURNED DAILY, AND THIS RUN IS A MATERIAL-CHANGE REVIEW RATHER THAN A CALENDAR ONE. TWO THINGS TRIGGERED IT. FIRST, THE HORMUZ CORRIDOR: dated 07-September reporting has Iran describing an arrangement with Oman to manage Strait shipping as days away, following a temporary route agreed in late August - the first documented de-escalation path in this conflict, though nothing is signed and the waterway has not reopened. SECOND, THE ALUMINA CORRIDOR: dated 12-September evidence shows Asia exporting 7.05 Mt of alumina in H1-2026, up 27.36% year on year, with India swinging to a 1.72 Mt trade surplus on exports up 51.3% and imports down 34.9%. THE CHINA-TO-WEST SEMIS CORRIDOR IS UNCHANGED AND REMAINS THE PRINCIPAL MECHANISM RELIEVING THE WESTERN SHORTAGE. REVIEW NOTE, 19-SEPTEMBER: this panel is reviewed monthly or on material change, not refreshed daily. It was reviewed this run and NO CORRIDOR HAS BEEN CHANGED. One development was weighed and rejected as insufficient: commodity reporting captured 18-September indicates a PARTIAL easing of Strait of Hormuz transit, with satellite imagery suggesting about 2.8 million barrels a day of Saudi crude moved through over six days against roughly 700,000 in August, alongside roughly 60 million barrels routed outside the strait via ship-to-ship transfer. That is crude, not metal, and the same reporting records only four commodity vessels detected transiting on the Thursday. A corridor is not re-rated on an adjacent commodity's partial recovery; it is re-rated when metal flow evidence prints. Aluminium Bahrain's confirmed routing via Jeddah and Sohar - around rather than through Hormuz - is consistent with the corridor remaining impaired.

flows.impact: Rising - and it is now the principal mechanism relieving the Western shortage
flows.note: Semi-finished exports 3.2 Mt in January-June, +18% year on year, with June at a record 695,000 t. Alloy exports nearly doubled to 238,500 t and China turned NET EXPORTER of aluminium alloy in June for the first time since 2019. Primary exports +32% to 38,400 t, much of it likely Western-origin bonded metal being redirected rather than Chinese production leaving. Driven by a tax structure that charges 30% on primary exports and zero on alloy and semis, and enabled by soft domestic demand - Citi's China end-use tracker fell 0.4% year on year while primary production rose 2.2%. The corridor consequence is that the Western physical shortage is being relieved WITHOUT unwrought metal changing hands, which is one public explanation for how a primary deficit can coexist with a flat or discounted LME front end.

flows.note: REVISED THIS RUN AND THE REVISION IS EXPLAINED. Dated reporting of 07-September-2026 has Iran saying an agreement with Oman to manage Strait of Hormuz shipping is days away, after more than three weeks of talks covering proposed inbound and outbound routes, the security and sovereignty of both states, and a proposed joint coordination centre; a separate 26-August report states a temporary maritime route had already been agreed. THE WATERWAY HAS NOT REOPENED: full reopening is reported as conditional on the United States fulfilling commitments under a June interim deal that has since lapsed, and no agreement is signed. THE ESCALATION FACTS ARE NOT DELETED - Iran said it attacked ten ships near the Strait and the United States said it sank five Iranian tankers. WHAT HAS CHANGED IS EVIDENTIAL CATEGORY, FROM UNCONFIRMED RUMOUR TO DATED MULTI-OUTLET REPORTING, AND THAT IS WHY THE CORRIDOR IS RE-RATED WHILE THE PHYSICAL POSITION IS NOT DECLARED REPAIRED. RE-RATED THIS RUN ON MATERIAL CHANGE. About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf production is exported through it. THE CORRIDOR RE-ESCALATED OVER THE WEEKEND after a week in which this page had carried a de-escalation: US strikes on two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on 30-August, Iranian retaliation against US bases, and an IRGC claim that a supertanker caught fire after striking naval mines. Brent rose 3.19% to $90.91 on it. President Trump stated on 01-September that strikes would be limited and the Strait is 'in very good condition' with large oil volumes moving; both statements are dated and both are carried. THE PHYSICAL POSITION BEHIND THE HEADLINES IS THE PART THAT HAS NOT CHANGED: Qatalum remains at roughly 60% of its 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas with no published restart timetable and a second Hydro force majeure outstanding; Alba has reduction Lines 1, 2 and 3 idled since March, 19% of 1,623 kt, with no announced restart and a stated intention to replace rather than restart them; EGA's Al Taweelah smelter is at 25% of cells with full production reaffirmed for Q1-2027. Gulf primary output ran roughly 40% below pre-war levels in April. This is the one corridor on the page where the disruption is both real and, in Qatalum's and Alba's cases, undated.
src: Bloomberg, 07-September-2026 - Iran says Strait of Hormuz deal with Oman just days away; Al Jazeera, 26-August-2026 - Iran and Oman agree temporary Hormuz route

A Hormuz routing agreement does not address this constraint. Saudi Arabia has been diverting crude to the Suez routing; the Suez leg for Gulf and Red Sea origin cargoes is therefore still not a clean alternative to Hormuz.

catalysts.text: THE NEXT LME OFFICIAL, DUE 13:20 LONDON, AND IT IS THE SINGLE MOST INFORMATIVE SCHEDULED EVENT ON THIS PAGE. There is no ring on Saturday or Sunday, so Monday's settlement is the first new information the exchange will produce. THE QUESTION IS BINARY AND THIS PAGE IS STATING IT IN ADVANCE: does the cash-to-three-month spread RE-WIDEN beyond $15.00, HOLD near flat, or CROSS into outright CONTANGO? A re-widening restores the tightness case and would lift the bull scenario back to 30%. A crossing into contango would be the first session this cycle on which the exchange stops paying for immediacy at all, and would raise the bear case. Watch the stock line with equal attention: a second consecutive zero, or a genuine BUILD, would confirm that the drawdown has ended rather than paused.

THE 3,261 LEVEL FACES ITS FIFTH CONSECUTIVE TEST AND ITS FIRST AFTER A WEEKEND. Three-month closed the week at $3,282.00, $21.00 above it, and has settled above it every session since 15-September. Weekend gaps are where levels that held on momentum get retested on fresh positioning. A daily settlement below 3,261 is the published condition for raising the bear scenario, and on the weekly Elliott count it is the level the position-degree structure turns on.

THE MONTHLY CARBON-INPUT SETTLEMENT CYCLE IS OPEN, OVERDUE AND HAS STILL NOT PRINTED. Prebaked anode, coal tar pitch and green petcoke marks normally settle around the 17th-18th of each month. Nothing has published into this window, so roughly a fifth of the smelter cash-cost stack is being carried on marks that are now about a month old. When it prints, the direction is signposted by a Brent that has now fallen three consecutive sessions to about $103.87 - but signposted is not the same as settled, and this page will append a mark to the input histories only when a dated public figure exists.

THE NEXT DATED STEP IN THE US-CANADA TARIFF SCHEDULE: a US vehicle and dairy import ban takes effect, following Canada's 50% counter-tariffs across CAD 27.6bn of imports in force since 08-September and the 08-September White House annex that lifted previously exempt downstream aluminium lines to a combined levy of up to 100%. This is a regional-delivered-price event, not an LME event: it moves US premiums and trade routing rather than the exchange price.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE QUARTERLY PREMIUM SETTLEMENT - STILL THE LARGEST SINGLE DATED EVENT LEFT ON THIS PAGE AND NOW ABOUT TWO WEEKS OUT. The pending range carried here is $280-310/t against a settled Q3 record of $395/t, a fall of 22-29% if it lands inside. The range is unchanged for a fifth consecutive run because no newer dated evidence has printed. THE NEGOTIATING BACKDROP MOVED AGAINST THE SELLER THIS RUN: the exchange backwardation collapsed to $3.00 and Aluminium Bahrain's restart was quantified at about 1.3 Mt annualised. Both are arguments a buyer can put on a table with a date and a source attached.

CHINA'S NATIONAL DAY HOLIDAY AND THE POST-HOLIDAY RESTOCKING TEST - THE CLEANEST FORWARD EXPERIMENT AVAILABLE ON CHINESE DEMAND. Dated 18-September analysis identifies pre-holiday restocking and a Xinjiang logistics bottleneck as the two drivers of the 63,000-tonne weekly ingot destock, and states plainly that both have built-in expiry dates. The test is therefore explicit: STRONG post-holiday restocking would mean the tightness was genuine demand; a MUTED return would confirm it was seasonal. Watch alongside it whether Xinjiang shipments normalise into coastal hubs, and whether the fifth-consecutive weekly build in cast alloy stocks - about 34,100 t against roughly 28,100 t in late August - finally breaks.

THE NEXT FEDERAL OPEN MARKET COMMITTEE MEETING. With the dot plot pointing to at least one further increase possible in 2026 after the 16-September move to 3.75-4.00%, the meeting is the next scheduled point at which the rates channel can re-intensify. The observed pass-through so far is small - a combined -0.21% on aluminium three-month across the two settlements that contain the decision - but the carry channel is visibly biting through a ten-year back at 4.997%, and carry is the channel that acts on the curve rather than the price.

risks.text: THE FEDERAL RESERVE IS A STANDING HEADWIND AND THE SECOND SETTLEMENT CONFIRMED THE FIRST - HELD AT FLAT. The Committee raised the target range 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16-September, unanimously, the first increase since 2023, with the dot plot showing one further increase possible in 2026. Across the TWO settlements that now contain the decision, aluminium three-month has moved a combined -0.21%. The dollar index moved 0.02% on 18-September and the LME euro fixing 0.11%, so the currency channel did essentially nothing. THE ONE CHANNEL THAT DID BITE IS CARRY: the US ten-year returned to 4.997% from 4.937%, giving back the previous session's relief within a day, and a five-per-cent financing cost is structurally hostile to a backwardation because nobody is paid enough to hold the stock a backwardation is meant to attract. The yield move and the spread collapse on the same session are consistent. The risk is real, persistent and now partly VISIBLE in the curve rather than the price - but it is not intensifying, so it stays flat.

THE GULF SUPPLY OUTAGE IS UNWINDING ON THE RECORD, IT HAS A TONNAGE, AND IT IS NOW THE MOST PLAUSIBLE PUBLISHED EXPLANATION FOR WHAT HAPPENED TO THE CURVE. HELD AT UP AND STRENGTHENED AGAIN. Aluminium Bahrain is running at about 1.3 million tonnes annualised on Lines 4, 5 and 6 - roughly 80% of a pre-war 1,623 kt plant - with exports moving via Jeddah on the Red Sea and Sohar in Oman, per its chief executive at the Fastmarkets Budapest conference on 16-September as reported 18-September; damage from the late-March Iranian strike was described as minor. Emirates Global Aluminium's Al Taweelah remains a partial restart at a publicly stated 18% of capacity with a return to previous output guided for early 2027. THE LINK TO THE BOARD IS DIRECT: on 18-September aluminium's backwardation collapsed to $3.00 while copper's front flipped INTO backwardation and zinc's widened, on a session with no dollar move. An aluminium-specific loosening of the front needs an aluminium-specific supply explanation, and returning Gulf tonnes are the one on the record.

TARIFF POLICY REMAINS THE DOMINANT DETERMINANT OF REGIONAL DELIVERED PRICE, BUT NOTHING ESCALATED THIS RUN, SO THE TREND IS CUT FROM UP TO FLAT. The Section 232 headline rate is re-verified and UNCHANGED at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives, with Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Taiwan and the European Union. The 08-September White House annex adding 50% to previously exempt downstream lines - producing a combined levy of up to 100% on some products - and Canada's 50% counter-tariffs across CAD 27.6bn of imports both remain in force but are eleven days old and are no longer new information. NO NEW TARIFF ACTION PRINTED INTO THIS WINDOW. The next dated step is a US vehicle and dairy import ban on 29-September. The LEVEL of this risk is unchanged and high - at $3,285.00 cash the 50% leg alone is about $1,642.50/t, which is why US premiums must be read as policy numbers - but a risk that is not moving is flat, and calling it rising without new evidence would be dishonest.

THE COST FLOOR IS FLAT TO FALLING ON THE ENERGY LINES AND SIMPLY ABSENT ON THE CARBON LINES, SO THE TREND STAYS FLAT. Brent fell for a THIRD consecutive session to about $103.87, with reporting attributing it to easing Saudi supply risk rather than weak demand; coal eased 0.45% to 144.00. Working the other way, European gas TTF rose again to about EUR 79.52, up about 1.17% on this page and 4.14% on the reference board, and it is the only clearly rising energy line - which matters specifically for Alunorte's TEMPORARY gas-supplier terminal-access agreement and Qatalum's reduced-gas curtailment. THE CARBON COMPLEX IS THE REAL GAP: prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petcoke normally settle around the 17th-18th of the month and NO NEW PUBLIC SETTLEMENT HAS PRINTED, so roughly a fifth of cash cost is being carried on marks that are now a month old. That is a data risk as much as a price risk and it is declared rather than smoothed over.

THE BACKWARDATION HAS NOW COLLAPSED RATHER THAN MERELY ERODED, AND THIS RISK IS RAISED FROM MEDIUM TO HIGH IMPACT. The four-run sequence is $21.00, $18.50, $18.50, $3.00 - an 84% fall in a single session and the fourth consecutive narrowing. The curve is within three dollars of flat. THIS PAGE NAMED THE PATTERN THREE RUNS AGO WHEN IT WAS STILL ARGUABLY NOISE AND STATED THE TEST; the test has now resolved against the tightness case. Two features make today's print harder to dismiss than the previous three. First, spread and flat price moved in the SAME direction, which removes the positioning-artefact explanation available when they diverge. Second, the LME stock draw stopped dead at exactly zero on the same session - the only flat print in the fifteen-session window - so the two independent daily measures of physical tightness went to nil together. WHAT WOULD TURN THIS BACK DOWN IS PUBLISHED AND SPECIFIC: a re-widening beyond $15.00 on a settled official. What would make it worse is a crossing into outright CONTANGO.

THE STOCK DRAWDOWN STOPPED DEAD, SO THIS RISK IS RAISED FROM DOWN TO FLAT. Yesterday this row was cut to DOWN because the draw had resumed at the fastest pace of the window, 1,000 tonnes. Today the reported change is EXACTLY ZERO and the line is unchanged at 242,600 tonnes - the only flat session in the fifteen-session window. A flat print is NOT a build and this page will not call it one; the level remains close to multi-decade lows and about 8,600 tonnes below the August monthly mean of 251,215. But the daily confirmation that visible tightness is still being consumed has gone, and it went on the same session the backwardation collapsed. The honest label is flat: the risk of a stock rebuild is neither receding nor yet materialising. The chart floor stays at 235,000 with 7,600 tonnes of headroom and is re-checked every run.

THE EX-CHINA RESTART PIPELINE IS NO LONGER JUST VISIBLE AND DATED - IT IS QUANTIFIED, SO THIS RISK IS RAISED FROM FLAT TO UP. The publicly reported list now carries a hard number at its largest line: Aluminium Bahrain at about 1.3 Mt annualised against a 1,623 kt plant. Alongside it, Century's Mt Holly is at full capacity for the first time since 2015 on a $50m investment restarting more than 50,000 t; Slovalco is restarting the first 75,000 t of 175,000 t guided for Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals has its first potline guided before end-2026 for about 75,000 t, with public reporting attributing the investment case to the 50% US tariff; and 18-September industry reporting frames a broader US rebuild spanning casting, electrolysis maintenance, scrap processing and metal quality, from a base of four operating smelters and about 660,000 t of 2025 primary output. SEPARATELY, EGA HAS LICENSED ITS DX+ ULTRA TECHNOLOGY TO NALCO for a proposed 500,000 t/y Angul expansion - a 2030s tonne, but a directional one. Restarts are slow and none of this lands this quarter; that is why it is Medium likelihood and Medium impact rather than High. But it is now rising, not flat.

A PREMIUM PANEL WHERE EVERY ROW IS CARRIED IS A DATA RISK IN ITS OWN RIGHT, AND ON A SATURDAY IT IS UNAVOIDABLE RATHER THAN NEGLECTED - HELD AT FLAT. This page compiles on SATURDAY 19-September. No price-reporting agency publishes a premium assessment on a Saturday, so no row in the premium panel CAN have moved since yesterday, and every row is carried at its last dated public mark with the as-of date stated. The oldest material carry is the CIF Japan spot indication at $370/t. The settled Q3 Japanese benchmark of $395/t is not stale - a quarterly benchmark is fixed until the quarter turns - but it is increasingly disconnected from dated September spot reporting of roughly $320-380/t. THE RISK THIS CREATES IS SPECIFIC: the Q4 settlement, due late September or early October, could reset 22-29% lower in a single print, and a reader looking only at the panel would see no warning in the numbers themselves. The warning is written here instead.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.
